text:
maria: Heads-up — noticing more model-serving 503s during GPU preemptions in eu-west1. Thinking we should introduce a small "eviction-buffer" of on-demand GPUs in mixed pools + a scheduling policy so critical pods move there first. thoughts?
jordan: +1 saw the spike yesterday. suspiciously the CA and drain are racing: pods get deleted from spot -> nowhere to land -> 503s.
kevin: we should avoid full mirrors. lightweight on-demand buffer (2-3 nodes) with a taint works well: taint buffer to keep normal pods off unless they tolerate it. then give critical classes toleration.
sam: agree. config knobs we should tune at the same time: cluster-autoscaler `scaleDownUnneededTime` and `maxPodEvictionTime`, and kubelet `evictionHard` maybe. also increase drain grace for model-serving. :thumbsup:
maria: any concrete taint/annotation pattern people have used?
jordan: we used `buffer.redwood.io/hold=true:NoSchedule` before. nodes get label `pool=warm-on-demand` and `eviction-buffer=true`. autoscaler node group weight set so CA prefers spots.
kevin: for lifecycle safety add a preStop hook on containers to flush KV/cache before pod SIGTERM. tiny snippet:```yaml
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/checkpoint && sleep 3"]
```
sam: also extend our termination-notice handler to delay node eviction by +10s when it sees GCP/AWS preempt notice so buffer can absorb transient spikes. node-problem-detector helps.
maria: cost question: 3 warm nodes in region is ~0.6x of spot price across baseline workloads — acceptable if it prevents the deploy from failing. propose start with 2 nodes and measure.
jordan: CA weights proposal: reserved/warm nodegroup priority 100, spot nodegroups priority 10. that makes CA scale down spots first.
kevin: remember to add PodDisruptionBudgets for the model-serving charts so CA won't evict below minAvailable. also ensure our webhook sets priorityClass for critical pods.
maria: action items: 1) infra: label/taint + create warm nodegroup (infra-bot) 2) eng-infra: update CA params (jordan) 3) runtime: add preStop to container images (kevin) 4) ops: monitor cost/eviction metrics 48h then decide (sam)
sam: I'll make a runbook PR with the key metrics: `node_preemptions`, `eviction_rate`, `fallback_on_demand_count`, `pod_restart_503s` and thresholds.
maria: ping @infra-bot when the nodegroup is created pls.
infra-bot: infra-bot: created INF-4123: "eviction-buffer rollout (eu-west1 canary)" and assigned jordan, kevin. https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-4123
jordan: starting canary now in eu-west1 with 2 warm nodes, will watch for 30m then 6h, posting metrics to #deploy-observability.
kevin: added preStop skeleton to runtime image branch `buffers/prestop` and opened PR.
maria: perfect — thanks everyone. if we see >1% cost increase we revert. otherwise iterate.
kevin: :thumbsup:
